claims.text: In 2021-2025, age-standardised cancer mortality in Åland was 2.4% above the national level (ratio 1.024, 95% interval 0.958-1.093), about 1.9 more deaths a year than its age structure predicts.
No measured pathway stage shows Åland clearly worse than the country; if outcomes differ, the cause is not locatable from public data.

Time from referral to diagnosis and from diagnosis to first treatment is not published by county for any cancer, so the Goal 3 indicator "patients access treatment within the established target times" cannot be checked from open data.

Recommended: standardised, timed cancer pathways with a fast-track referral. Under the stated assumptions this postpones about 1.4 deaths a year in Åland (range 0.2-2.8) for an assumed EUR 46,254 a year; it stayed in the portfolio in 94% of sensitivity runs.
First step for every county: Add first contact, referral, diagnosis and first treatment dates, plus entry route, to the national cancer quality register and publish county-level medians quarterly.
